advice.claim: Touchless services are beneficial because they do not increase labor costs per dollar of service.
advice.quote: I think the primary thing that I love about touchless, just like we've loved about our business for so long is that we don't have increased labor associated with every dollar of service which is very traditional in old-school wellness so

advice.claim: When expanding your offerings, ensure the core business remains intact and the new additions do not detract from the original service.
advice.quote: So it's super important that when you're looking at adding wellness or expanding your wellness, that your main core is structured in a way that when you add to it, it doesn't take away from it.

advice.claim: Train staff to use specific terminology that focuses on the experience rather than just the service.
advice.quote: we're going to train our staff to say it this way it's not going to be unlimited it's not going to be tanning it's about a sun experience a sun session versus tanning

advice.claim: Ensure your core business remains strong and well-structured before adding new services or expanding your offerings.
advice.quote: it's super important that when you're looking at adding wellness or expanding your wellness, that your main core is structured in a way that when you add to it, it doesn't take away from it.

advice.claim: Ensure your core tanning equipment is modern and high-quality before marketing new wellness services.
advice.quote: Get your house in order before you add to it.

advice.claim: Update your entire brand identity, including decor, marketing, and staff presentation, when pivoting to a wellness-focused model.
advice.quote: if you just change your name and put a wellness behind it but don't change anything don't do anything and don't invest in your business change your marketing change the way you present yourself from the front desk staff to the way your salon is decorated to your marketing to your social media

advice.claim: Outsource social media content creation to a professional agency to maintain a consistent and high-quality presence.
advice.quote: So what I did was I hired a company that takes video. We actually hired a modeling agency and Negotiated a rate with them and we just had it booked every two weeks that we were doing photo photo and video shoots

advice.claim: Use key performance indicators (KPIs) to determine the lifetime value of a customer to structure staff incentives properly.
advice.quote: it's absolutely imperative that you know what a customer is worth to you over a lifetime and even over the next 12 months and then to structure your incentives accordingly

advice.claim: Offer high incentives to staff for signing up members because the high profit margin and long-term commitment make the upfront cost worthwhile.
advice.quote: if you have a membership for instance a high incentive to sign up that member upfront is worthwhile because if you know that you're going to get 16.8 months of that membership at $69 then you could afford to give a whole bunch upfront

advice.claim: Manage the business using KPIs and provide appropriate incentives to staff.
advice.quote: So I think managing the business with KPIs and then incentivizing those properly and highly is important, very important.

advice.claim: Use personalized gestures like handwritten cards and gift bags to improve staff retention and morale.
advice.quote: So me and Kelsey handwrite a card for every girl on their birthday and their anniversary with us.

advice.claim: Create a welcoming environment for new hires by having the entire team send a welcome message.
advice.quote: they get 41 messages back welcoming them so I didn't realize the impact that that was making until they_They know how great that was and how much they shared with their parents.

advice.claim: Offer non-monetary rewards like reward points for reliable behavior and community involvement to motivate staff.
advice.quote: so really what I did is took everything that my staff are doing that was driving me crazy and put it into a positive so if you have a perfect month which means you did not call in sick you did not change a shift you did not all the things when it comes to showing up that we would just take for granted of course you get a perfect month you get you get reward points for coming in, staying late, bringing product from one store to another, doing something good in the community on your anniversary.

advice.claim: Run internal competitions for staff to drive membership sign-ups and upgrades.
advice.quote: we have a contest, and we really found that doing it against themselves instead of each other so that changed probably about 10 years ago so again they get uh you know three points for an all-access sign up and then they get two points for an upgrade and then they get to buy things from that

advice.claim: Adjust staff pay structures if they are too close to minimum wage to ensure staff feel valued.
advice.quote: So my last two years have focused on the hourly wage. So now my big girls make $32 to $34 an hour because I listened and then I had to adjust to that.

advice.claim: Use a tracking list to ensure you are giving attention to consistently good staff members who might otherwise be overlooked.
advice.quote: So I really make sure that my middle children get attention, the ones that just are consistently great.

advice.claim: Update your management practices even if you have always done them a certain way.
advice.quote: All these challenge fields, just because you've always done it that way doesn't mean that it's the right way for today. If you have to adjust the way that you're paying your staff, do it.

advice.claim: Lead your team by asking about their personal lives to understand what might be affecting their performance.
advice.quote: you need to lead them not tell them so I'm always about showing up and like Lisa said how are you doing today what's going on what's happening in your life because they may have something that's going on in their life that's affecting what's going on in their job

advice.claim: Provide staff with skills and education that they can use for their entire careers to build a positive culture.
advice.quote: But when I'm teaching them something, make sure they know that this isn't just for here. Like, you know, I'm going to tell you something real, you learn this together. But you are going to use this for the rest of your life.

advice.claim: Establish a consistent feedback culture to address and correct employee behavior before it becomes ingrained.
advice.quote: I think creating a feedback culture where feedback is consistent all the time is imperative. If you leave behavior unaddressed for weeks at a time, or months at a time, you can expect the behavior to get worse and harder to change.

advice.claim: Be direct and firm about dress code standards to ensure staff feel confident and professional enough to sell.
advice.quote: you have to look like you care because you can't sell and be confident if you don't feel that way, which our job is sales.

advice.claim: Use uniforms to eliminate guesswork for staff and create a cohesive brand image.
advice.quote: It takes the guesswork out of that uniform. Getting dressed in the morning. It makes it easier for them to come to work and go back to what they're wearing in the morning.

advice.claim: Provide staff with clear visual examples and specific guidelines regarding their uniforms to ensure a consistent brand image.
advice.quote: I gave a very very clear example in our own wording of what they should look like.

advice.claim: Offer alternative uniform options to ensure staff of all sizes and preferences feel comfortable and included.
advice.quote: I have an alternative to that. That's important right? Very, very important

advice.claim: Establish non-negotiable standard operating procedures for staff training and appearance.
advice.quote: So when you're training, make sure you have your standard operating procedures. These are the non-negotiables.

advice.claim: Instead of asking staff what is in a product, ask them to identify specific clients who would buy it.
advice.quote: Instead of telling me what's in that product, I want to know one or two clients that would buy those products.

advice.claim: Implement memberships to ensure consistent revenue and offer additional services like wellness.
advice.quote: Well, I think everybody's going to say if you don't have memberships, that's the first thing you need to do. Memberships are absolutely the way you have to go, and you can always bring in wellness for that membership.

advice.claim: Prohibit the use of outside products in the salon to protect equipment and ensure safety.
advice.quote: do not let any other lotion other than what you sell be used in your stores I do it it is a non-negotiable

advice.claim: Require customers to leave their own products at the front desk and provide them with a sample instead to ensure they use your approved products.
advice.quote: Just give them one of those, and let them use your lay down, and make them leave their bottle at the front desk, they'll love you forever.

advice.claim: Conduct regular evaluations of all staff members to ensure they are committed to the business and meet your standards.
advice.quote: do a serious evaluation of every one of your team members and really make sure that they're all team members that want to be on the bus and if they're not have those tough conversations to either improve their performance to the standards that you want them to be or help them move on to the next career

advice.claim: Build a talent pipeline by networking in your community to ensure you have replacement candidates ready if a staff member leaves.
advice.quote: Your job as salon owners to recruit new staff is to build your bench.

advice.claim: Use social media to showcase your salon's culture to attract potential employees.
advice.quote: advertise your culture. When you look at your socials and things like that, You want people in your community to want to work there, right?

advice.claim: Include a link to join your team on your social media profiles to attract applicants.
advice.quote: it is either the link for his business website or to join his team oh i like that that is spectacular because that is where our employees are they're on instagram so i just had to say that was something i'm going to do
